"""Face-state lifetime and caller-output staging experiments; no new precision.

Serial faces recompute the algebraic J stream from one shared log seed and
repeat the edge potentials. They trade arithmetic for fewer live face states.
Staging explicitly uses the caller's final output allocation for 26 raw tensor
accumulators, trading global traffic for live registers; no scratch allocation.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import re
from types import SimpleNamespace
import warp as wp
import fluxbridge_shared_jk_shortmath as seeds
import fluxbridge_shared_jk_layout as geometry
import fluxbridge_shared_jk_stability as paired

BASES=('control','serial','staged','serial-staged')
VARIANTS=tuple(v+(f'@{cap}' if cap else '') for cap in (None,192,160,128) for v in BASES)


def source(variant='control'):
    kind=variant.split('@')[0]
    if kind not in BASES:raise ValueError('unknown variant')
    code=seeds.source('balanced')
    if kind.startswith('serial'):
        start=code.index('Face f0=face_data(');end=code.index('// C_1=',start)
        old=code[start:end];seed=old[old.index('T j_even='):]
        seed=re.sub(r'\bj_even\b','j_even_seed',seed);seed=re.sub(r'\bj_odd\b','j_odd_seed',seed)
        code=code[:start]+seed+'''for(int side=0;side<2;++side){
 Face f0=face_data(ids[2+side],2*edge+side);
 T j_even=j_even_seed,j_odd=j_odd_seed;
'''+code[end:]
        code=code.replace('m0+=f0.d*f0.w*f0.p+f1.d*f1.w*f1.p;','m0+=f0.d*f0.w*f0.p;')
        code=code.replace('mL+=f0.d*f0.w*f0.pL+f1.d*f1.w*f1.pL;','mL+=f0.d*f0.w*f0.pL;')
        code=re.sub(r'consume\(ids\[3\],2\*edge\+1,f1\.[^;]+;','',code)
        code=code.replace('consume(ids[2],2*edge,f0.d','consume(ids[2+side],2*edge+side,f0.d')
        code=re.sub(r'T t1=[^;]+;','',code)
        code=re.sub(r'f1\.\w+(?:\*=|\+=|=)[^;]+;','',code)
        assert 'f1.' not in code
        pos=code.index('T C=');code=code[:pos]+'}\n'+code[pos:]
    if 'staged' in kind:
        names=['m0','mL']+[n+'.'+a for n in ('m1','G') for a in 'xyz']+[p+s for p in ('b','v','h') for s in ('xx','xy','xz','yy','yz','zz')]
        aliases={n:f'LD(output,{i},row)' for i,n in enumerate(names)}
        old='float m0=0,mL=0;struct A{float x,y,z;};A m1{0,0,0},G{0,0,0};'
        new='struct A{volatile float &x,&y,&z;};\n'
        new+='volatile float &m0='+aliases['m0']+',&mL='+aliases['mL']+';\n'
        for n in ('m1','G'):new+='A '+n+'{'+','.join(aliases[n+'.'+a] for a in 'xyz')+'};\n'
        assert old in code;code=code.replace(old,new)
        for prefix in ('b','v','h'):
            pattern=r'float '+prefix+r'xx=[^;]+;'
            replacement='volatile float '+','.join('&'+n+'='+aliases[n] for n in names if n.startswith(prefix) and '.' not in n)+';'
            code,n=re.subn(pattern,lambda _:replacement,code);assert n==1
        pos=code.index('auto consume=')
        code=code[:pos]+''.join(n+'=0;\n' for n in names)+code[pos:]
        pos=code.index('T C=')
        # Snapshot all raw tensor slots before writing the final, differently
        # indexed output. Volatile staging prevents accidental register caching.
        snapshot='{\nfloat m0='+aliases['m0']+',mL='+aliases['mL']+';\nstruct Final{float x,y,z;};\n'
        for n in ('m1','G'):snapshot+='Final '+n+'{'+','.join(aliases[n+'.'+a] for a in 'xyz')+'};\n'
        for prefix in ('b','v','h'):snapshot+='float '+','.join(n+'='+aliases[n] for n in names if n.startswith(prefix) and '.' not in n)+';\n'
        code=code[:pos]+snapshot+code[pos:]
        code+='\n}\n'
    return code


@lru_cache(None)
def functions(variant='control'):
    if variant not in VARIANTS:raise ValueError('unknown variant')
    cap=int(variant.split('@')[1]) if '@' in variant else None
    api=geometry.functions('float32');vec,real=api.vec,api.real;Geometry=paired.split_geometry_type()
    @wp.func_native(source(variant))
    def interaction(x:vec,h:real,tet:int,output:wp.array2d(dtype=real),row:int,g:Geometry)->real: ...
    @wp.kernel(module='unique',cuda_max_registers=cap,module_options={'enable_backward':False,'fuse_fp':True,'max_unroll':1})
    def baseline_w6(particle:wp.array(dtype=vec),support:wp.array(dtype=real),tet:wp.array(dtype=int),g:Geometry,output:wp.array2d(dtype=real)):
        i=wp.tid();ignored=interaction(particle[i],support[i],tet[i],output,i,g)
    return SimpleNamespace(**{**vars(api),'Geometry':Geometry,'kernel':baseline_w6,'channels':28})

"""Sustained matched lifetime/cap configurations with rotating order."""
import argparse
import fcntl
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import statistics
import numpy as np
import warp as wp
import fluxbridge_shared_jk_lifetime as impl
import fluxbridge_shared_jk_stability as paired
from fluxbridge_shared_jk_full_study import arrays
from fluxbridge_shared_jk_consumers import scene
from fluxbridge_single_term_study import ROOT


def main():
    p=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__);p.add_argument('--output',type=Path,required=True);p.add_argument('--configurations',default='control:256,control@128:256,serial:128')
    a=p.parse_args();a.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    with open('/tmp/fluxbridge-gpu.lock','a') as lock:
        fcntl.flock(lock,fcntl.LOCK_EX);wp.init();device=wp.get_device('cuda:0')
        report=dict(device=device.name,pairs=1048576,block_dim=blocks[v],launches_per_batch=32,rounds=3,samples_per_round=7,rows=[],
            scope='Per-launch CUDA-event duration of 32 sequential graph launches; preallocated identical buffers; rotated variant order each round; no profiler',
            source_sha256={str(f):hashlib.sha256(f.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for f in (ROOT/'scripts/studies').glob('fluxbridge_shared_jk*.py')})
        configuration=[(v,int(b)) for v,b in (c.split(':') for c in a.configurations.split(','))];variants=[v for v,b in configuration];blocks=dict(configuration);n=report['pairs'];report['configurations']=configuration
        if len(variants)!=len(set(variants)) or any(v not in impl.VARIANTS or b not in (32,64,128,256) for v,b in configuration):raise ValueError('invalid configurations')
        for mixed in [False,True]:
            vertices=scene(mixed);g=paired.prepare_geometry(vertices,device,'floatpair-inline');rng=np.random.default_rng(852)
            ids=rng.integers(0,len(vertices),n,dtype=np.int32) if mixed else np.zeros(n,int)
            if mixed:
                edges=(vertices[:,1:]-vertices[:,0,None,:]).transpose(0,2,1)
                q=vertices[ids,0]+np.einsum('nij,nj->ni',edges[ids],rng.uniform(-.5,1.5,(n,3)));h=rng.uniform(.3,2,n)
            else:q=.2+rng.uniform(-.015,.015,(n,3));h=np.ones(n)
            args,out=arrays(impl.functions('control'),g,q,h,ids,device);graphs={};initial={}
            for v in variants:
                api=impl.functions(v);wp.launch(api.kernel,n,inputs=args,device=device,block_dim=blocks[v]);wp.synchronize_device(device)
                initial[v]=out.numpy()
                with wp.ScopedCapture(device=device) as cap:
                    for _ in range(report['launches_per_batch']):wp.launch(api.kernel,n,inputs=args,device=device,block_dim=blocks[v])
                graphs[v]=cap.graph
            # Warm every graph, keeping both kernel and clocks active before
            # collecting the rotating-order rounds.
            for v in variants:wp.capture_launch(graphs[v])
            wp.synchronize_device(device)
            for round in range(report['rounds']):
                for v in variants[round:]+variants[:round]:
                    samples=[]
                    for _ in range(report['samples_per_round']):
                        start=wp.Event(device,enable_timing=True);end=wp.Event(device,enable_timing=True)
                        wp.record_event(start);wp.capture_launch(graphs[v]);wp.record_event(end);wp.synchronize_event(end)
                        samples.append(wp.get_event_elapsed_time(start,end)/report['launches_per_batch'])
                    stable=bool(np.array_equal(out.numpy(),initial[v]));assert stable
                    report['rows'].append(dict(mixed=mixed,round=round,variant=v,block_dim=blocks[v],event_samples_ms_per_launch=samples,median_ms=statistics.median(samples),graph_bitwise_equal=stable))
                    a.output.write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2,allow_nan=False)+'\n')
                    print(mixed,round,v,statistics.median(samples),flush=True)


if __name__=='__main__':main()

diagnostics: Initial serial prototype incorrectly omitted compact edge-potential contributions for a zero-w face; fixed before final gates by consuming each face even when w=0. Exact edge-line singular path remains unchanged.

Initial output-staging prototype had a closing-scope compilation error; corrected before final CPU/CUDA gates. Initial batch driver had a metadata initialization error, corrected before collecting batches.

Extending only the permitted register-cap list from 128 down to 96/80/64 and correcting batch metadata changed study source hashes; exact earlier successful source versions are archived and verified above. Numerical kernel generation for existing variants did not change.
Output staging trades register lifetime for explicit global output-buffer reads/writes; no additional scratch allocation; it loses to the moderate-cap control and is not recommended.
limitations: Only the independent 116-case full-output fixtures are CPU-validated for all four distinct mathematical bodies; register caps alter CUDA allocation only and are validated on CUDA, not redundantly on CPU.
Additional 81920 actual-input cases use analytic fp64 reference; two worst cases cross-check exact inputs against previously converged independent oracle values.

Primary sustained batches rotate order over three seven-sample rounds, each sample containing 32 launches; mixed timings vary. Keep all ranges and matched controls; clocks/power/desktop activity uncontrolled.
Compiler local allocation bytes/thread are not traffic volume; sector bytes/pair are measured local L1 requests, not DRAM bytes.
Highest occupancy is not the fastest kernel. Further register caps increase spills and can reduce both arithmetic issue efficiency and throughput.
Kernel-only matched timing; excludes preparation, search, material assembly and transfers. Input/output and split geometry allocations remain unchanged; compiler spill storage is separate.
Experimental register cap, serial-face and staging variants do not constitute a generally valid raw-fp32 analytic implementation or solver integration.
conclusion: Register pressure is a real speed bottleneck in the paired core. A 128-register cap doubles achieved occupancy to about 33%, raises canonical issue utilization from 37% to 68% and gives about 1.79x canonical / 1.38x mixed sustained throughput despite moderate cached spill traffic. A 160-register cap is also competitive for mixed work; 64 registers increases occupancy to about 61% but loses performance. Keep 128/160 as explicit experimental performance controls while conditioning/narrowing the radial arithmetic.
